- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) or shows strong volatility, model often underestimates or misses upward spikes; increase forecast for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 70+ price peaks) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.6 to -0.4), model often fails to adjust quickly — delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and apply gradual adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price increases (last 7–10 days) — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast tail if sentiment is positive or neutral.
